opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer. He requested admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so as a full-time employee without ownership, his maximum is write. Admin is above the maximum, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a contractor with basic security training per the Security DB. Contractors with basic training max out at read (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed). He requested admin to Payroll, which is above the max, so I recommend granting read.
reason: Timothy Wallace (E022) requested admin access to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR notes full-time Engineer (max write for Payroll, since Engineer does not own Payroll), while the Security DB notes contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training, admin never allowed). Under either interpretation, admin is above the maximum, and the more restrictive valid maximum is read. Granting read stays within policy under both sources.
